firstMismatch.source: Mounted boulder failure message omitted by moverock_core obstructed-destination caller; all RNG and cursors match.

summary: The accepted v90 case diverges only when a mounted lawful Knight tries to push a boulder into an obstructed destination: C prints the steed's sentence-initial name and the push refusal, while JavaScript omits the message after taking a named unported-callee path. The source owner is hack.c:cannot_push_msg, with required production caller wiring in hack.c:moverock_core.

source.branch: In moverock_core, when the destination is out of bounds, obstructed (including a wall), iron bars, a blocked diagonal door, or another boulder, C calls cannot_push_msg(otmp,sx,sy) before returning cannot_push(); cannot_push_msg chooses the mounted YMonnam(steed) message when u.usteed is set, then calls feel_location when Blind. The same helper is called by the closed_door destination branch. The production route is cmd.c:rhack -> hack.c:domove_core -> test_move(DO_MOVE) -> moverock -> moverock_core.
dependencies: do_name.c:YMonnam -> y_monnam (1133-1139): existing JavaScript do_name.js YMonnam/y_monnam implementation provides the mounted steed name
pline.c:pline (message output): existing JavaScript ttyPline message path
display.c:feel_location: existing JavaScript feel_location path for blind heroes

evidence: Accepted-base provenance: v90 manifest names this mission as hack.c:cannot_push_msg mounted branch through moverock_core obstructed-destination caller. Its listed first mismatch is segment 0, step 43, key h, comparison base 93fa87a40ed6219b5d31e211f22b460af55bfe92. The admitted evaluation reports 43/44 screens, 2717/2717 RNG values, and 44/44 cursors; the divergent C cell is Y (color 8) and JavaScript cell is space (color 8).

Pinned C source at nethack-c/upstream revision 16ff59115315917b93185d026aeefea06db9b0f4: src/hack.c:247-261 cannot_push_msg calls pline("%s tries to move %s, but cannot.", YMonnam(u.usteed), what) when mounted, otherwise You(...); Blind additionally calls feel_location. The whole src/hack.c:moverock_core definition is lines 348-646; it calls this void helper for closed_door at 486 and the failed destination conjunction at 633 before returning cannot_push. Its normal production route comes from test_move(DO_MOVE) at 1222-1230 and moverock at 336-345.

At accepted JavaScript source, js/hack.js:1900-1911 cannot_push_msg explicitly throws UnsupportedHeroMoveBoundaryError for state.u.usteed instead of producing the mounted C message. js/hack.js:2444-2445 and 2519-2520 also skip this helper for mounted heroes and record note_unported('hack.c cannot_push_msg') in the matching closed-door and obstructed-destination branches. The v90 mismatch specifically takes the latter branch; this is a source gap, not an RNG, cursor, or renderer discrepancy.

Implementation scope is the whole hack.c:cannot_push_msg source unit plus required caller wiring in hack.c:moverock_core, keeping its existing cannot_push return behavior. JavaScript already imports y_monnam from do_name.js; it can form the C sentence-initial name with upstart(y_monnam(steed,state)). Existing ttyPline and feel_location utilities cover the other source effects. No new naming or message dependency is needed.

The admission evaluation's manifestSha256 is the cases corpusDigest, not a raw manifest-file hash. scripts/challenge-results.mjs defines it over sorted {id,recordingSha256} entries; that corpus digest is 9ac16f693445b5f757427adee430b199d6ce01156910dd959e95bce1c972769d and matches the saved evaluation. The unchanged raw challenges/manifests/v90.json bytes hash to cb785f6887f617437b4e4fb54a641b0db93a1bc9ee5091b50aff66675dc2a93a. This is an expected distinction, not an evidence blocker.
